page.text:
The final primary connective is *negation*, written $\neg P$ and read
*not $P$*. Unlike conjunction and disjunction, which are binary
operations combining two arguments, negation is a unary operation acting
on a single statement. It acts as an involution on truth values: if $P$
is true, $\neg P$ is false; if $P$ is false, $\neg P$ is true. Under
classical bivalence, asserting $\neg P$ is entirely equivalent to
asserting that $P$ fails to hold.
